newsitem.title: USA: Long-time Standard Federal president dies.
newsitem.headline: Long-time Standard Federal president dies.

text.p: Standard Federal Bancorp said Tuesday that Thomas Ricketts, its long-time chairman and president, had died Tuesday morning from abdominal cancer.

Ricketts, who was 66, joined Standard Federal in 1956 after graduating from the University of Michigan School of Law. He was named to the firm's top executive position of president and managing officer in 1974 and became chairman in 1981.

Under his tenure, the 104-year-old Standard Federal grew into a stockholder-owned financial services company with a retail banking network in several Midwestern states and a wholesale mortgage leading operation throughout the United States.
Ricketts, who underwent surgery for the cancer earlier this month, most recently oversaw Standard Federal's $1.9 billion sale to the Dutch firm ABN AMRO Holding NV.

The deal, for $59 a share in cash, was the largest acquisition of a thrift in terms of purchase price in industry history, according to the company. Standard Federal shareholders voted last week to approve the deal.
At the end of March Standard Federal, which is based in Troy, Mich., had assets of $15.8 billion and deposits of $11.5 billion.
Ricketts' death came one month after his wife of 40 years, Priscilla, died from injuries she suffered after being struck by a car in a parking lot. The incident remains unsolved.
Ricketts was active in numerous civic organisations, including serving on the boards of the Detroit Symphony Orchestra and the Economic Club of Detroit.
Other survivors include a son and daughter, a grandson and a brother.
